audit.whatIsWrong: Galio's R was called "Idol of Durand" and credited with pulling and taunting under a damage-reduction shield.
audit.why: Riot's kit: W is Shield of Durand (charge, damage reduction, releases a taunt); R is Hero's Entrance — Galio designates an ally's position, shields allies in the area, then slams down and knocks up. No pull, no taunt on R. Also Counter Strike (E) dodges all incoming ATTACKS, so Winds of War, the W taunt release and Justice Punch all land through it.
audit.corrected: Renamed R to Hero's Entrance everywhere, moved the taunt onto W, and stated that Counter Strike dodges attacks only so none of Galio's CC misses.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's R was written as "Grandmaster at Arms"; Galio's R cooldown was never given.
audit.why: Jax's R is Grandmaster's Might (110/100/90s) — third-strike magic damage plus an Armor and MR steroid. Galio's Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s, the longest cooldown in the matchup and the reason the side-lane duel is yours.
audit.corrected: Real R name used and Hero's Entrance's cooldown named in the late-game and foe-wants text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart said Jax at Levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items; the packet chart and every "why" string say Galio controls levels 2 through the first item.
audit.why: 49.81% over 1319 games with prose that reads "it stays his to control", "he keeps every extended trade" and "he holds the lane even through your first item" — the sides contradicted the text and the packet chart.
audit.corrected: Rows 2 through first item flipped to Galio in both layers as one atomic group; 2+ items stays Jax.

audit.why: Justice Punch at 11s rank 1 is the punishable cooldown and the page already keys commits to it.

edits.before: His biggest window: Justice Punch (E) knock-up into Idol of Durand (R) channel — the R is the part that pulls you in and taunts, with a big damage-reduction shield up, and it's his cue to flash-R onto you with a jungler attached.
edits.after: His biggest window: Justice Punch (E) knocks you up, then Shield of Durand (W) taunts you out of the follow-up, and Hero's Entrance (R) is the ally-targeted slam that shields his side and knocks you up again with a jungler attached.

edits.before: His spike, not yours: Justice Punch (E) into Idol of Durand (R) pulls you in and taunts you under a damage-reduction shield and calls his jungler — a clean kill setup you can't dodge with Counter Strike.
edits.after: His spike, not yours: Justice Punch (E) knocks you up, Shield of Durand (W) taunts, and Hero's Entrance (R) drops an ally on you behind a shield — Counter Strike dodges attacks only, so none of that CC ever misses.

edits.before: This is his window, not yours. At 6 his Justice Punch (E) into Idol of Durand (R) is a dash-knockup into a channeled AoE that PULLS you in and taunts you — the pull is on the R, not the W — while a big damage-reduction shield eats everything you throw, and it's his cue to flash-R for the jungler. The honest read: your Counter Strike stun does nothing against the taunt CC itself, and the R/W reduction blunts your Empowered autos, so even with Trinity Force you trade roughly even while he out-sustains and out-tanks you. Bait the W taunt and Justice Punch out, give nothing while they're up, and only commit Q-W-E in the gap when both are on cooldown.
edits.after: This is his window, not yours. At 6 his Justice Punch (E, 11s at rank 1) dash-knockup sets up Shield of Durand (W) — the taunt is on the W, not the R — and Hero's Entrance (R) is the ally-targeted slam that shields his side and knocks you up when the jungler arrives. The honest read: Counter Strike dodges incoming attacks only, so the taunt, the knock-up and Winds of War all land straight through it, and W's damage reduction blunts your Empowered autos — even with Trinity Force you trade roughly even. Bait the W and Justice Punch out, give nothing while they're up, and only commit Q-W-E when both are on cooldown.

edits.before: Now you take over. Once Blade of the Ruined King and your R (Grandmaster at Arms) Armor/MR steroid come online, your on-hit DPS and stacking attack speed cut through his armor and stacked magic resist the way no single combo could earlier, and in a side lane his R (Idol of Durand) has a long enough cooldown that you win the 1v1 once it's spent. Drag him to a side lane and force the extended duel — that's the one place his global R and AoE taunt do the least and your sustained on-hit does the most. Just respect that if his team groups, his R is a game-state ult, so take the duel where he can't get peel.
edits.after: Now you take over. Once Blade of the Ruined King and your R (Grandmaster's Might) Armor/MR steroid come online, your on-hit DPS and stacking attack speed cut through his armor and stacked magic resist the way no single combo could earlier, and in a side lane Hero's Entrance (R) is on 140s even at rank 3, so you win the 1v1 the moment he spends it. Drag him to a side lane and force the extended duel — that's the one place his global R and W taunt do the least and your sustained on-hit does the most. Respect that if his team groups his R is a game-state ult, so duel him where he gets no peel.

edits.before: Hold Counter Strike for his passive-empowered autos and minion aggro, not for the W taunt or R — neither is an auto you can dodge
edits.after: Hold Counter Strike for his passive-empowered autos and minion aggro, not the W taunt or R — it dodges incoming attacks only, never abilities

edits.before: Charge W (Shield of Durand) and release the taunt as you commit, or land E (Justice Punch) into R (Idol of Durand) to lock you in a chunk you can't dodge
edits.after: Charge W (Shield of Durand) and release the taunt as you commit, or land E (Justice Punch) into Hero's Entrance (R) to lock you in a chunk you cannot dodge

edits.before: Hold his global R (Idol of Durand) to roam mid/bot and snowball off your lane being even, not lost
edits.after: Hold Hero's Entrance (R, 180s at rank 1) to roam mid/bot and snowball off your lane being even, not lost

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Galio's Justice Punch is down.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges his autos but never the W taunt. Only take the trade when Justice Punch (11s) is down.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Galio's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance lands an ally on you behind a shield, so 6 is his level, not yours — fight only when Justice Punch is already spent.

notes: Galio's R is Hero's Entrance, not "Idol of Durand" — the invented name appeared in spikes[1].text, whys[4], mid, late and wants.foe[0]/[2], and it carried an invented mechanic (an R pull-and-taunt). The taunt is Shield of Durand (W). Jax's R is Grandmaster's Might, not "Grandmaster at Arms". Level chart flipped rows 2 through first item to Galio to match the packet chart and the existing why-strings.
